messages:
Jordan (support): Heads-up, multiple support tickets from EU customers reporting streaming sessions that stop mid-response (partial outputs) around the 8–12s mark, then the client reconnects and gets duplicate tokens. Seen across both hosted and dedicated tenants.
Jordan (support): Examples from customers: one saw a truncated assistant reply, another saw a second resumed chunk that repeated the last sentence. Several include 499 / client closed logs on our edge and a flurry of reconnects.
Maya (customer-success): Reports mainly from eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. A few big customers (SaaS + fintech) are getting pretty upset — asked for ETA and mitigation.
Jordan (support): I collected traces -> attached short snippet in case it helps:
```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate"
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< ...
* recv fail: Connection was reset, errno 104
```
Jordan (support): On our side logs show upstream wrote finish frames then connection reset with TCP RST from the LB in a few cases.
Tanvi (oncall): @alex can you check LB/lightweight proxy timeouts? This smells like keepalive or idle timeout mismatch between proxy and client.
Alex (sre): On it. Pulling logs for LB and nginx edge pools. Any correlation with batching spikes?
Emily (prodeng): We saw a small spike in long-running streams at 16:32 UTC in EU. Could be a slow token/kv cache eviction path triggering backpressure. I'll look at runtime metrics for that window.
sre-bot: Incident assigned to #oncall-tanvi (sev:high) — auto-created page.
Tanvi (oncall): Added. Quick checklist: 1) Confirm which layer is closing tcp 2) Reproduce with curl from eu region 3) Roll temporary fallback 4) Notify customers with workaround.
Jordan (support): Repro steps from customer repro: they post a ~2k token prompt, accept SSE, stream starts, then after ~8–12s stream stops, client reconnects and sends resume request -> our endpoint accepts and sends the rest, but some middleware duplicates what was already delivered.
Alex (sre): Found multiple RSTs from LB to edge in the timeframe. Timeouts show upstream idle timeout 30s, client idle vs chunk gap often ~10s which is fine. But we have an intermittent proxy bug where intermittent premature FIN is sent when connection seen as ‘zombie’ due to incorrect socket reuse.
Emily (prodeng): Can you paste the LB logs from one sample trace id 0e7a5f?
Alex (sre): Paste: 
```
[0e7a5f] client_ip=1.2.3.4 request=/v1/streams/generate status=499 up_reason=RST upstream_write_err=1 backend=edge-42
```
Alex (sre): Looks like upstream write error -> the edge process tried to write but socket closed by LB. Need to correlate with kernel-level socket close events.
Tanvi (oncall): Immediate mitigations we can try (short term):
- Increase LB keepalive and idle timeouts to 90s for EU pools.
- Disable HTTP/2 connection pooling on the problematic proxy temporarily to avoid socket reuse bug.
- Add server-side dedupe of resumed chunks by tracking last-token-id per stream (cheap guard).
- Enable non-streaming fallback (poll) for affected customers if they want immediate reliability over latency.
Maya (customer-success): I'll message the top 3 affected accounts with the fallback steps and offer a workaround to switch to non-stream mode; they prefer quick stability.
Jordan (support): Customers asked for a status page update. Suggest posting a targeted note: "Investigating EU streaming interruptions; temporary workarounds: retry/resume cadence and non-stream fallback; mitigation in progress."
Tanvi (oncall): I'll open an IMO on status. Also plan to push a hotfix to edge to dedupe on resume — low-risk.
Emily (prodeng): Quick patch checklist: add idempotency check on stream resume (compare last-delivered-token-id), log resume gaps, and add metric. I can review PR.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued for edge-hotfix/stream-resume-dedupe -> staging -> canary.
Alex (sre): While deploy runs, I'm going to bump LB idle timeouts and disable HTTP/2 pooling for EU. Rolling now across EU pools.
Jordan (support): Noted. Customers asking about billing — are we double-billing for resumed tokens?
Emily (prodeng): We currently bill on tokens emitted by model. If resume duplicates tokens due to middleware re-send, billing may count duplicates depending on where we dedupe. Need to run a query on billing events for the traces.
Jordan (support): I'll tell them we're investigating potential duplicate billing and will refund if any duplicates are confirmed. Keep me posted.
Alex (sre): LB change rolled to eu-west and eu-central. Early telemetry: reconnects down ~60% on eu-west in the past 12 minutes.
Tanvi (oncall): Canary of edge-hotfix succeeded. Rolling to 25% traffic. Watching for chunk duplication metrics.
Emily (prodeng): Adding a temporary routing rule: heavy streaming sessions > 60s get routed to dedicated streaming pool (bypasses the buggy proxy) until full rollout is done. This should reduce exposure.
Maya (customer-success): Customers on the support thread are okay with temporary reroute to dedicated, one asked for an ETA. I'll update: ETA for full fix ~3–6 hours, monitoring in place.
Jordan (support): Customer asked for repro steps to validate fix from their side — suggested they force long prompts and verify no truncated replies, or they can enable non-stream fallback.
Tanvi (oncall): Current status: LB timeout increased, HTTP/2 pooling disabled, dedupe patch rolled to 25%, routing rule applied for long streams. Next: roll dedupe to 100%, validate billing duplicates, run postmortem.
Alex (sre): Confirming no kernel OOMs or socket exhaustion on edge nodes; the root cause seems to be proxy socket reuse bug + occasional upstream write race. We'll include stack traces in the postmortem.
Emily (prodeng): Postmortem owner? I can own the fix and perf verification. Tanvi can own the incident timeline.
Tanvi (oncall): I'll own the postmortem write-up. Please dump relevant logs and screenshots into the incident doc.
Jordan (support): I'll draft initial customer notification and include workaround instructions + offer credits for impacted windows.
Maya (customer-success): Thx. Let me know when dedupe is at 100% and we can close the customer-facing incident.
Tanvi (oncall): Closing note for now: mitigation working, customers notified, ongoing monitoring. Will update in 30m or earlier if rollback/issue. :white_check_mark:
